plugins.name: Design

plugins.description: Three skills for polished UI: clean-ux, motion-ux, and minimal-ux. Minimal-ux adds dark themes, 3D coverflow galleries, and click-to-open detail panels.
plugins.author: LottieFiles · Design System
highlights: Design tokens: colors, typography, spacing & radius
Components: buttons, cards, modals, sidebars, tabs
Motion: timing, easing & choreography tables
Disney animation principles adapted for UI

skills.name: clean-ux
skills.author: Design System
skills.description: Visual design language for all UI output. Every component, layout, and page should follow the design specs in the module files — tokens, typography, buttons, cards, accordions, sidebars, modals, and more.

skills.name: minimal-ux
skills.author: Copilot Research
skills.description: Light and dark editorial/agency UI with GSAP/Lenis motion, 3D coverflow galleries, and click-to-open detail panels.

skills.name: motion-ux
skills.author: LottieFiles
skills.description: Applies motion design principles to create emotionally-driven, technically sound animations. Provides timing, easing, choreography, and Disney animation principles adapted for UI. Works with CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, Lottie, or Spring.

plugins.name: Notch Companion App
plugins.tagline: Build native macOS apps that live under the MacBook notch.
plugins.description: Playbook for building lightweight, native macOS "notch companion" apps — agent apps (no Dock/menu-bar icon) that hide under the MacBook notch and react to the cursor with fluid, physics-driven animation drawn in code. Covers building without Xcode (SwiftPM + hand-assembled .app), a transparent click-through overlay over the notch, a 0%-idle-CPU animation loop, spring/Verlet physics + gesture systems, global mouse monitors, context menus, code-drawn art & app icons, headless testing, and DMG/GitHub distribution. Use when building NotchPaw or any variant (e.g. a pull-chain that locks the screen, a notch pet, a notch gauge/widget, a peeking character).
plugins.author: NotchPaw
highlights: Build without Xcode using SwiftPM + a hand-assembled .app
Transparent, click-through overlay pinned under the notch
0%-idle-CPU animation loop with spring / Verlet physics
Global mouse monitors, context menus & DMG distribution

skills.name: notch-companion-app
skills.author: NotchPaw
skills.description: End-to-end playbook for lightweight macOS notch companion apps: transparent overlay over the notch, cursor-reactive physics animation, global mouse monitoring, code-drawn art and icons, headless testing, and DMG/GitHub distribution.

plugins.name: Film Crew
plugins.tagline: A full crew — researcher, writer, designer, sound, subtitler and publisher — that turns a topic into a finished film.
plugins.description: A film crew for making videos. Give the director a topic and a style and it runs the whole production: a screenwriter researches it and writes a script where every spoken fact carries two sources, a story editor engineers the hooks and open loops, a voice booth narrates it, a storyboard artist plans a visual beat every few seconds, and a production designer shoots it in a chosen style — archival paper collage or a broadcast news bulletin, with more added as folders. Cuts vertical Shorts from the hookiest moments, packages everything for YouTube, and publishes only what a human has approved. Also assembles long recorded sessions into episodes and Shorts.
plugins.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
highlights: One command: /director --paper --topic “…” --shorts 3 --parts 2 --publish
Fifteen stages, fourteen crew skills — discovered from the filesystem, never hard-coded
Every visual style is a skill of its own; installing one adds a look and changes no code
Research, sound, captions and rights clearance are separate roles with their own gates
Publishing needs approval bound to the exact bytes; re-render and it lapses

skills.name: director
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Runs the whole production. Parses the brief, picks or ranks the style, fans the work out into episodes and Shorts, and drives the crew stage by stage — refusing to call anything done without an artifact behind it, and refusing to publish without approval bound to the exact file.

skills.name: head-of-marketing
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Packages a finished video for YouTube: a searchable bilingual title, description, chapters and tags, a thumbnail built to survive a 168px search result, a subscribe-and-bell outro, and limit linting against every field YouTube will reject. It writes the package; it never uploads it.

skills.name: production-designer
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Owns the look. Holds the style registry, ranks styles against a topic, compiles a beat plan into the chosen style's storyboard and renders it. A style is just a folder, so new looks drop in without code changes — and a style that cannot draw what a beat asks for says so rather than substituting something close.

skills.name: publisher
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Uploads to YouTube and nothing else. Publishing is the one irreversible step in the plugin, so every upload, edit, thumbnail and privacy change is gated on an approval bound to the sha256 of the exact bytes a human saw — re-render the file and the approval lapses rather than carrying over.

skills.name: researcher
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Establishes what is true before anyone writes a sentence. Two independent sources per claim, verbatim quotes stored, contradictions recorded rather than resolved, and gaps written down so nothing gets asserted just because it sounded right.

skills.name: rights-manager
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: The last gate before an upload that cannot be taken back: every asset's licence and attribution on record, and every figure and superlative in the title checked back against the ledger. Refuses by default; exceptions must be reasoned and recorded.

skills.name: screenwriter
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Turns the researcher's ledger into narration that is accurate to the second and to the fact: every line bound to a claim, contested numbers left hedged, sized to the runtime budget before the first sentence is written, and linted before it counts as a deliverable.

skills.name: sound-designer
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Decides what the film sounds like underneath the voice: mood, music bed, ducking keyed to the narration envelope, and one final mix whose loudness is measured and reported rather than assumed.

skills.name: story-editor
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Engineers a script so people keep watching — the opening three seconds, the open loops that hold the middle, and an ending that earns a rewatch. Hook taxonomy, re-hook vocabulary, cut-rhythm and caption specs, and the rules for writing narration a neural TTS engine can actually perform, enforced by a linter.

skills.name: storyboard-artist
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Turns a finished script into a beat plan: what appears on screen, on which spoken word, and which moments are worth cutting as Shorts. Deliberately style-neutral, so the same plan can be shot in any style — with a validator that checks pacing, that on-screen keywords are actually spoken, and that every open loop is paid.

skills.name: style-news
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: A rolling news bulletin — full-bleed footage under a stacked kicker and headline, channel bug and location chip. Suits journalism, business and breaking events.

skills.name: style-paper
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: A documentary researcher's pinboard — aged paper, torn photographs, typewriter labels and one red pen. Suits history, disaster, investigation and science.

skills.name: subtitler
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Writes the caption file the platform actually indexes — timed from the rendered storyboard, broken at clauses for reading speed, and spelling the proper nouns the way the ledger spells them instead of the way a recogniser guesses them.

skills.name: tn-assembly
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Turns one long assembly or parliament webcast into a set of publishable videos. Detects highlights and heated exchanges from the audio, derives how many episodes the session actually justifies, cuts every segment on natural speech boundaries at full resolution, and builds branded long-form episodes plus vertical Shorts that route viewers back.

skills.name: voice-booth
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: Generates natural-sounding voiceovers and narrations using edge-tts. Creates high-quality neural audio files from text, with pacing and pauses tailored for video production, and measures every clip so the storyboard can be timed against it.

plugins.name: Product Launch
plugins.tagline: Turn a raw demo recording into a polished launch video.
plugins.description: Turns a product demo recording into a polished, motion-designed product launch video. Probes and reviews the footage, tightens dead air, assembles the best moments, then adds a branded intro, synced feature captions, transitions, a logo bug, an outro CTA, and a final logo + name end-card, plus an original synthesized music bed and UI sound effects. Cross-platform engine (ffmpeg + Python: Pillow + numpy) that runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux, with an optional macOS-native Swift/AVFoundation fast path. Use when someone asks to create a launch / promo / teaser / "show-off" / Product Hunt / social video from a screen recording or product demo. ALWAYS ask the user for a demo recording (and any missing product details) the moment this skill is triggered if they were not already provided.
plugins.author: product-launch skill
highlights: Probes footage & tightens dead air automatically
Branded intro, synced captions, logo bug & outro CTA
Original synthesized music bed + UI sound effects
Cross-platform ffmpeg + Python, optional Swift fast path

skills.name: product-launch
skills.author: product-launch skill
skills.description: Assembles the best demo moments and layers on a branded intro, synced feature captions, transitions, a logo bug, an outro CTA, an end-card, plus a synthesized music bed and UI SFX — rendered with a cross-platform ffmpeg + Python engine.

plugins.name: Azure — Skill as Compute
plugins.tagline: Rents an Azure VM for the heavy part of a job, then destroys it.
plugins.description: Skill as Compute — rents an Azure VM for the heavy parts of a job and gives it back. Any skill can hand a compute-intense task to a burst machine with one command: it sizes the VM to fit a monthly budget, installs the Azure CLI and signs in if needed, ships the working directory up, runs the work there, brings the results back, and destroys the whole resource group. A watchdog on the machine deletes it even if the laptop dies, so nothing is left running. Use it to offload video rendering, encoding, TTS, batch image work or long builds instead of melting the local machine.
plugins.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
highlights: One call: offload — create, upload, run, download, destroy
Sizes the machine to a monthly budget (default ₹10,000, shown in USD)
Live Azure retail pricing; steps down to a smaller VM rather than overspend
Three independent ways the VM dies, including a watchdog that deletes it if your laptop does not
Installs and signs in to the Azure CLI by itself; detects Spot and GPU restrictions before deploying

skills.name: azure-compute
skills.author: Vignesh Ramamoorthy
skills.description: The way any other skill borrows compute. Hands a compute-intense task to a temporary Azure VM sized to fit your budget, runs it there, brings the results back, and deletes the whole resource group.
